article.title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
article.summary:

The UK Antarctic Heritage Trust (UKAHT), a Cambridge-based charity, is in its second year of a three-year mission to save Port Lockroy.
This year's team will install beams and props to help the buildings withstand increased precipitation and snow loading, as well as monitor the penguins.

article.title: Electricity generation per person in the United Kingdom has fallen by a third from its early-2000s peak

article.title: Here's How US Recycling Companies Are Turning Old Wind Turbine Blades Into Cement
article.summary:
Wind turbines are great for generating clean energy, but they have a life cycle of, at most, around 20–30 years.
However, wind turbine blades aren't easy to recycle, as they are made from fiberglass, a material that is difficult and expensive to break down.
Fortunately, recycling companies have found a variety of ways to recycle around 85% of a wind turbine blade, one of which is turning it into concrete and cement.
By breaking down turbine blades, it's possible to recover materials and fibers that are useful for concrete production.
A study published in 2024 concluded that fibers from wind turbine blades can strengthen concrete.

article.summary:
Palestinians have been displaced from their homes in Tulkarem refugee camp and dream of returning home.
This West Bank camp he can see in the distance once housed a two-storey building comprising four apartments, each measuring 300 square metres (3,229sq feet), in which he and his extended family lived.
Everything changed for Fuad and his family on January 21, 2025, when Israel launched a military assault in the occupied West Bank dubbed “Iron Wall”, initially targeting the Jenin refugee camp.

article.title: Nigel Farage says Reform will suspend the UK asylum system for five years and deport thousands of refugees if he becomes PM
article.summary:
Nigel Farage today pledged to ban anyone from being granted asylum in the UK for five years if Reform wins the next election.
The Reform UK leader re-ignited a proposal from earlier this year to suspend the asylum system for a full parliamentary term and declare void any applications in progress.
All asylum tribunals, legal refugee routes and resettlement schemes will be scrapped and a Reform government would not hear the around 90,000 outstanding asylum and humanitarian protection appeals and instead deport the claimants.
Reform says there is 'no mandate' for such schemes and that anyone who has arrived under them would be deported.
But Reform is now expanding the toolkit of measures for countries that would not be hit hard by such restrictions.

article.title: Miliband says Britain won't tolerate threats on our soil, as Iran ambassador summoned
article.summary:
The foreign secretary has summoned the Iranian ambassador to make clear that "Britain will not tolerate threats on our soil" following last month's incident at RAF Fairford.
Ed Miliband said attempts by Iran to undermine the UK's security "through its criminal networks, proxy groups and state-backed malign activity is unacceptable".
Iran's ambassador to the UK, Seyed Ali Mousavi, said Tehran was not involved and was willing to cooperate with British authorities.
In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".
RAF Fairford, in the Cotswolds, has been used as a forward operating location by the US air force for decades.

article.title: It is inconceivable to think Russia did not try to interfere in Brexit vote, says PM
article.summary:
Andy Burnham has said it is "inconceivable" to think that Russia did not try to interfere in the 2016 EU referendum.
The prime minister told MPs he had not been questioning the legitimacy of the Brexit vote when he told the Rest is Politics podcast that it was "clear" there had been interference by Moscow.
His comments to the podcast provoked angry responses from some Brexit campaigners, with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage calling the prime minister "a liar".
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the prime minister had "implied that the referendum result was illegitimate because of Russian interference".
He also urged the prime minister to publish evidence of interference in the Brexit referendum as well as other UK votes.

article.title: The world's hottest AI stock market has gone cold
article.summary:
South Korea's stock market has gone from the world's hottest to its coldest in just a few months.
The Kospi, the world's best-performing major stock benchmark in the first half of 2026, has since fallen about 24%, making it the worst-performing major market in the second half.
But investors are increasingly looking beyond South Korea's memory-chip giants to companies with broader exposure to the AI hardware boom.

Its market offers exposure across AI infrastructure, from advanced chip manufacturing and packaging to servers and networking equipment.
